title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This handwritten page is on the back of a typed SGA 7 IX sheet; the neighbouring pages are SGA 7 text, not part of this argument. It is a lemma and its corollary from Grothendieck's notes on the 'simplicial de Rham complex with divided powers' (Cor. 1.5).

(1) Lemma. Let A_*, B_* be simplicial k-modules and C_* the associated chain complex (boundary ∂_n = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i ∂_i).
- By Dold–Kan/Dold–Puppe, π_*(A_*⊗B_*) = H_*(C_*(A_*⊗B_*)).
- By Eilenberg–Zilber, C_*(A⊗B) is chain-homotopy equivalent to C_*(A)⊗C_*(B).
- Replacing A_*, B_* by chain-homotopic or quasi-isomorphic complexes A^!, B^! with good (flat) terms, the homology of A^!⊗B^! is computed by Künneth.
- In the case at hand B_* = Λ^iΨ_* with (Λ^iΨ_*)^! ≃ k[i]. Hence π_ℓ(A_*⊗Λ^iΨ_*) ≅ H_{ℓ−i}(A_*) = π_{ℓ−i}(A_*).

(2) Cor. 1.5. Consider the bigraded simplicial divided-power de Rham (Koszul) complex A_*^{p,i} = Γ^{p−i}(Φ_*) ⊗_k Λ^iΨ_*, with total degree p and exterior degree i. Implicitly:
- Φ_* is a contractible simplicial k-module, e.g. a cone, with Φ_* → Ψ_* surjective with kernel k, so Ψ_* ≃ k[1].
- Hence Λ^iΨ_* ≃ k[i]. This is the décalage LΛ^i(M[1]) ≃ LΓ^i(M)[i] applied to M = k.
- Γ^n of a contractible module is contractible for n>0 (Dold–Puppe: Γ^n preserves simplicial homotopy), while Γ^0 = k.
- Therefore π_ℓ(A^{p,i}) ≅ π_{ℓ−i}(Γ^{p−i}Φ_*), which is k if ℓ = i = p and 0 otherwise.

Consequence: for fixed p, the pieces A^{p,0}, …, A^{p,p−1} are acyclic ('flasques', in Grothendieck's usage). The only non-acyclic piece is A^{p,p} = Λ^pΨ_*, with π_p = k.

Purpose: to show that the simplicial de Rham–Koszul complex Γ^{*}Φ⊗Λ^{*}Ψ of a contractible-onto-K(k,1) situation behaves like a resolution concentrated on the diagonal. This is a building block for comparing a simplicial or derived divided-power de Rham complex with its expected cohomology (the theme of the 1976 IHÉS talk). It is essentially the mechanism behind Illusie's décalage isomorphisms and the acyclicity of divided-power Koszul complexes.
errors: He cites 'Dold–Puppe' for π_* = H_*(C_*); this is the Dold–Kan normalization theorem. Dold–Puppe is relevant only for the homotopy invariance of Γ^n and Λ^i.
The parenthetical calling A^{p,0},…,A^{p,p−1} 'des résolutions de k_*' conflicts with the computation itself, which shows they are acyclic (all π = 0). Only the total row behaves like a resolution.
'Flasques' is used nonstandardly to mean acyclic/contractible.
The key input Λ^iΨ_* ≃ k[i] (décalage) is asserted without proof. It requires Ψ_* to be degreewise flat with Ψ_* ≃ k[1].
The hypotheses on Φ_*, Ψ_* (contractibility of Φ, Ψ ≃ k[1]) are implicit and not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Computation of π_* of a tensor product of simplicial modules via Eilenberg–Zilber, Dold–Kan and Künneth
ideas.where_published: Standard; e.g. Illusie, Complexe cotangent I
Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations I, Ch. I §4.3

ideas.what: Bigraded simplicial divided-power de Rham/Koszul complex Γ^{p−i}Φ⊗Λ^iΨ and its acyclicity off the diagonal
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power Koszul complex; simplicial de Rham complex with divided powers (cf. derived de Rham / crystalline comparison)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (1971); Berthelot (PD de Rham); Bhatt (derived de Rham, 2012)
ideas.where_published: unsure; the 1976 IHÉS lecture itself is unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1976 programme of a 'simplicial de Rham complex with divided powers' anticipates the later derived de Rham ≃ crystalline philosophy. The computation here, that rows are acyclic except on the diagonal, is the local engine of such a comparison. On this page, though, it is only standard Koszul/décalage material.
missed.quote: Considérons p.ex. le complexe simplicial De Rham à puissances divisées A_*^{**} ≃ Γ^*(Φ_*)⊗_k Λ̇Ψ_*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents that Grothendieck pursued a simplicial PD-de Rham formalism around 1976, predating Bhatt's derived de Rham/crystalline comparison. The mathematics on this page itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a routine Eilenberg–Zilber/Künneth/décalage computation, essentially in Illusie's thesis. It is mildly interesting only as evidence of Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 simplicial PD-de Rham project.
transcription_corrections: 'B_*^! → B_* à un homologie[?]' should likely read 'B_*^! → B_* un homologisme' (a quasi-isomorphism), paired with 'A_*^! ≃ A_* chaîne-homotopisme'.

Under the line H_ℓ(A_*⊗B_*^!) ≃ H_{ℓ−i}(A_*^!), the second annotation should be π_{ℓ−i}(A_*) rather than π_{ℓ−i}(A_*⊗B_*). The annotations identify H_ℓ with π_ℓ(A_*⊗B_*) and H_{ℓ−i} with π_{ℓ−i}(A_*).
The phrase '(qui sont des résolutions de k_*)' is attached to the components in degree < p, or possibly is a marginal comment on the whole row.
The superscript annotations are 'degré total' (for p) and 'degré ext' (for i).
